BiblicalUsage: Methusael appears once, in the genealogy from Enoch to Lamech: Enoch begat Irad, Irad begat Mehujael, Mehujael begat Methusael, and Methusael begat Lamech. He is a link in the line of Cain, named only as a father and a son.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that even a single-verse name matters: Methusael stands in the line that leads to Lamech, and his place in the genealogy is the whole of what Scripture tells us about him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
